title: Why Sanitary Tees Fail on Horizontal Drain Lines
description: Installing a standard sanitary tee on a horizontal-to-horizontal drainage run is a common installation mistake that frequently causes chronic blockages. Sanitary tees are designed primarily for transitioning from horizontal to vertical flow, or for vent connections. When placed horizontally, the short radius sweep fails to direct solid waste smoothly along the pipe flow line, leading to stranded debris and splashing that disrupts proper venting. Professional codes require a combination wye and one-eighth bend or a long-sweep wye for horizontal direction changes to maintain proper flow velocity and prevent clogs.

Why Sanitary Tees Fail on Horizontal Drain Lines

Installing a standard sanitary tee on a horizontal-to-horizontal drainage run is a common installation mistake that frequently causes chronic blockages. Sanitary tees are designed primarily for transitioning from horizontal to vertical flow, or for vent connections. When placed horizontally, the short radius sweep fails to direct solid waste smoothly along the pipe flow line, leading to stranded debris and splashing that disrupts proper venting. Professional codes require a combination wye and one-eighth bend or a long-sweep wye for horizontal direction changes to maintain proper flow velocity and prevent clogs.
